title: UK PPI — December 2026 including services, October to December 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET): the quarterly SPPI edition, the last UK producer-price release the publisher has given a firm day
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/producerpriceinflationukdecember2026includingservicesoctobertodecember2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Producer price inflation, UK: December 2026 including services, October to December 2026', 'Release date: 20 January 2027 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', with no cancellation notice. Cadence independently reproduced from the publisher's own previous-releases listing (lowercase slug), fetched the same day: 'December 2025 including services, October to December 2025 — Released 21 January 2026' — the December reference month carries the quarterly services rider every year and publishes in the third full week of January. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Proposed twice on 2026-09-09, by the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2027-01-20 and by that of uk-ppi-2026-12-16
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-10, superseding BOTH proposals for this id — proposals/uk-ppi-2027-01-20.from-uk-cpi-2027-01-20.json and proposals/uk-ppi-2027-01-20.from-uk-ppi-2026-12-16.json — each read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. BOTH PROPOSALS' CLAIMS SURVIVE; three things are new. NEW 1 — THE MPC TEST MOVES UP A DOCUMENT CLASS, AND ONE HALF OF THIS RELEASE IS CITED AT ZERO. The uk-ppi-2026-12-16 lane showed three Monetary Policy Summary and minutes documents cite no producer-price term. Minutes are short; the Monetary Policy Report is 100 pages with a costs-and-prices chapter, and this print lands 15 days before the 2027-02-04 MPR round (Bank of England upcoming-MPC-dates page, fetched direct 2026-09-10: '4 February — includes Monetary Policy Report', published as 2027 provisional). Both the July 2026 and February 2026 MPRs were downloaded and text-extracted in full this session (200 pages, ~352,000 characters). Word-boundary counts: 'SPPI' 0, 'services producer' 0, 'factory gate' 0, 'PPI' 0. 'producer price(s)' appears ONCE in each pair — in July 2026 about CHINA ('the deflation in producer prices that had been present in the Chinese economy'), and in February 2026 the single UK citation, 'Further down the supply chain, producer output prices have been flat since August', inside the FOOD-inflation paragraph beside the Bank's Agents. So the honest statement is not 'the MPC never reads producer prices' but this: goods OUTPUT prices reach the MPR at roughly one citation per 100-page report, as a corroborating aside; the SERVICES producer price index — the only thing that makes this release different from every other UK PPI print — reaches it NEVER. And the July 2026 MPR shows why: it runs its own oil pass-through study by local projections on CPI components ('these results are not currently suggesting unusually large second-round effects') rather than reading the producer index at all. NEW 2 — THE HOSTILE BASE WAS A ONE-MONTH EVENT. The uk-ppi-2026-12-16 lane called the flat base over at its own print. The ONS December 2025 bulletin, fetched direct this session, shows the base turns friendly again immediately: input index 156.9 at m/m -0.2% for December 2025, against 157.2 at +0.5% for November 2025. So delta(annual rate, this print vs 2026-12-16) = (Dec-2026 m/m) + 0.2pp, and the annual rate RISES unless first-week-December Brent in sterling falls more than ~2.2% from first-week-November at the ~9.2% effective beta. Same bulletin also revises the sibling's own base: November 2025 was published as 157.1 / +0.3% in the November-2025 bulletin and reads 157.2 / +0.5% here, a 0.2pp move in the base that ledger's stall call rests on. NEW 3 — A LIVE SUPPLY SHOCK THE SIBLINGS DO NOT CARRY. Between their assessment (2026-09-09) and this one, Brent rose from $101.21 to $108.94 in one session (+7.6%, Yahoo BZ=F, 2026-09-10 23:29 UTC) on US-Iran strikes and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities; VIX 16.46 -> 17.84. At GBPUSD 1.3510 that is GBP 80.64, +48.6% on the July 2026 first-week average of GBP 54.25. Base case at today's spot: input +9.6% y/y (band 6.5-13.5%), output ~+4.9% (band 4.2-6.0%), the input-output gap widening to ~4.7pp. THE SERVICES HALF: the Q4 2025 base quarter is q/q +0.8% (ONS March 2026 bulletin, revised up from +0.7%), exactly the six-quarter non-spike norm, so annual SPPI = the Q3 2026 rate + (Q4 2026 q/q) - 0.8pp and the base does not bind. The record +1.8% Q2 2026 quarter does NOT roll out of the annual window here — it rolls out at the Quarter 2 2027 edition, published ~July 2027. Base case Q4 2026 SPPI 3.9-5.0%, centred ~4.3%. CALENDAR BOUNDARY, VERIFIED BOTH WAYS: this is the LAST UK PPI release the publisher has given a firm day. ons.gov.uk/releases/producerpriceinflationukjanuary2027 reads 'Provisional release date: February 2027' — month only, no day — while ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukjanuary2027 reads 'Provisional release date: 17 February 2027 7:00am'. The same-minute CPI/PPI pairing this chain has now verified on six consecutive release pages (09-16, 10-21, 11-18, 12-16, 2027-01-20 and the retired ones) cannot be extended to 2027-02-17 from the publisher; it can only be inferred, which is why no uk-ppi-2027-02-17 is proposed here.
